item.title: Afghan woman to fight U.S. efforts to deport her over "alien terrorist" claim
item.description: Nazira Haji Zada's lawyer argued that the Justice Dept. is violating her due process rights.

item.title: Father convicted in Apalachee High School shooting gets 15 years
item.description: Days after his son was sentenced, the father of the Apalachee High School shooter Colt Gray, is in court for his own sentencing hearing.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy jury hears from first responders about night her children died
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is facing three first-degree murder charges, accused of killing her children in her Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in 2023. Thursday was the third day of witness testimony.

item.title: Trump says he may pull Blanche's nomination until 2 Senate critics leave office
item.description: President Trump said Todd Blanche will remain acting attorney general as a holdup on his nomination continues.

item.title: Grants halted at agency devoted to safety of U.S. healthcare
item.description: Congress appropriated $345 million for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality for the 2026 fiscal year, but the agency has spent less than $15 million on grants.

item.title: White House doubles down on Trump's claims that China interfered with elections
item.description: The White House continues to claim that China interfered in U.S. elections, despite election experts disputing those allegations. China has denied interfering in the elections. CBS News election law expert and political contributor David Becker has more.

item.title: Poland suspects Russia violated NATO airspace rules; Moscow blasts Ukraine with missile barrage
item.description: Russia launched deadly strikes on Ukraine, killing at least eight people, including three children, officials say. Across the border in Poland, authorities are investigating an apparent Russian missile crossing into Polish airspace. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has more.

item.title: Netanyahu says he defers to Trump on Iran war expansion but differences may remain
item.description: The U.S. and Iran again exchanged strikes amid growing concerns that the war will expand to other parts of the Middle East. This comes as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that the future of the Iran war is up to President Trump. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports and contributor Elliot Ackerman shares his analysis.

item.title: Does homeowners insurance cover HVAC replacement? This is what's actually included.
item.description: Your homeowners policy may offer more HVAC protection than you think, but the fine print makes all the difference.

item.title: Iran war appears to expand to Egypt's coast as drones hit gas port
item.description: Drone strikes hit gas vessels at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean, as a poll shows little American support for the five-month war with Iran.

item.title: U.S. launches strikes on Iran after attempted missile attacks against American forces
item.description: American fighter jets launched air strikes against Iran after the attempted missile attacks on U.S. forces in Jordan. It comes after President Trump vowed to hit back and as the war in the Middle East widens. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: European teams boycott FIFA over plan to sell World Cup stake to investors
item.description: A source close to Joshua Kushner's firm tells CBS News there's no politics behind FIFA's bid to draw private investment, but Europe's soccer powerhouses are crying foul.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning": The Money Issue (Aug. 2)
item.description: This week Jane Pauley hosts "The Money Issue," our annual special broadcast dedicated to the many ways in which money underscores the way we live.

item.title: Several companies tied to Trump and his family distance themselves from controversial IRS agreement
item.description: Several businesses with ties to President Trump are distancing themselves from a controversial tax settlement involving the Internal Revenue Service. CBS News' Jake Rosen has the scoop.

item.title: Battle against monster wildfire in France boosted by improving weather
item.description: George and Amal Clooney are among thousands of residents in southwest France still displaced by a massive wildfire, but crews are gaining control.

item.title: OpenAI's Sam Altman meets with key White House advisers to discuss AI development
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is meeting with high-ranking Trump administration advisers following his talks with lawmakers on Capitol Hill. This comes as some tech workers criticize the rapid development of AI, demanding that the government create new safety regulations. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent has more.

item.title: Jared Leto denies sexual misconduct allegations made by multiple women in new BBC documentary
item.description: Multiple women accused performer Jared Leto of sexual misconduct in a new BBC documentary. Leto denies the allegations. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more details.

item.title: U.K. village plans independence vote in protest over migrant housing plans
item.description: The English village of Piddington is planning a symbolic referendum to demand independence from the U.K. over plans to house people seeking asylum at a disused military barracks.

item.title: Can you negotiate medical debt before it's sent to collections?
item.description: Your medical bills may be more flexible than you think. Here's what to know before you pay any balances.

item.title: Jury hears chilling 911 call from Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband in murder trial
item.description: A Massachusetts court heard disturbing 911 audio and key testimonies in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial. Clancy is accused of killing her three children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Newsom's taxpayer-funded California diaper program could "lead to waste," state records warned
item.description: Records reveal repeated warnings that Baby2Baby's plan to send every baby home with 400 diapers in limited sizes could lead to waste. The other finalist offered more diapers, more sizes and a direct-to-consumer option.

item.title: What records reveal about Newsom's taxpayer-funded, California-branded free diaper program
item.description: CBS California Investigates reviewed 356 pages of state records behind California's $6.2 million diaper contract with Baby2Baby. Here is what they show.

item.title: U.S. economy slowed in second quarter as Iran war weighs on growth
item.description: Economic activity weakened between April and June as energy costs surged, new government data shows.

item.title: White House levels new allegation that China swept up voter data
item.description: The Trump administration on Thursday reiterated its view that China's alleged efforts to collect millions of American voter registration files constituted election interference.

item.title: Why are workers at leading AI companies calling for a slowdown in AI development?
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and other AI leaders say they support pacing the rapid advancement of AI's capabilities.

item.title: Trump-affiliated companies distance themselves from Trump-IRS deal
item.description: Top Senate Democrats sought answers about Trump IRS deal from mining company Kaz Resources, cryptocurrency companies World Liberty Financial and prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi.

item.title: Newsom's office called our diaper contract reporting "demonstrably false." State records show what happened
item.description: Gov. Newsom's office says the no-bid deal was "competitive," the records weren't delayed, and our reporting is false. The state's own database, deadlines, and the Legislature's budget bills say otherwise. Here's the point-by-point review.

item.title: Newsom's "competitive bid" diaper deal wasn't. California's budget includes dozens of similar no-bid exemptions.
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom said the $6.2 million Baby2Baby contract "went through a competitive bidding process." State records reveal it didn't. CBS California Investigates found dozens of similar no-bid deals in the state budget worth over $1 billion.

item.title: California still hasn't released Baby2Baby diaper contract as lawmakers weigh longer public records delays
item.description: The Newsom administration waited 24 days to decide if it would even let Californians see the multi-million-dollar contract with Baby2Baby, a nonprofit linked to First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom.

item.title: Critics got California's free diaper math wrong, but state won't release key Baby2Baby records
item.description: A CBS News California fact-check found the state's free diaper program won't cost taxpayers 50 cents per diaper, as viral posts claimed. But the Newsom administration still won't release the Baby2Baby contract or competitive bid records amid concerns free diapers could go to waste.
